strengths: R2E provides a coherent, NLP-relevant contribution: entity-specific retrieval, masked answers, and set-based scoring make passage-level Shapley attribution tractable. Training with missing-evidence embeddings supports the interventions used for attribution.

The ranking results support the approach beyond frequency correction alone. On Gene Description Facts, uncorrected R2E achieves MRR 0.202 versus 0.167 for MLM and 0.176 for mean cosine similarity. Temporally held-out literature experiments also demonstrate improvements and benefits from updating the retrieval corpus without retraining.

The clinical literature experiment uses training from scratch and pre-2005 evidence, providing a meaningful retrospective evaluation. R2E retains MLM-level discrimination while providing evidence attribution: AUROC 0.632 versus 0.630. Analyses restricted to diseases with genetic insight strengthen the comparison with the genetics baseline.

The architecture, hyperparameters, splits, attribution algorithm, prompts, ablations, and computational costs are extensively documented. The three evaluation datasets provide useful community resources. These elements support a focused Findings contribution.
weaknesses: Practical explanation quality is less firmly established than score attribution. Shapley values explain the scoring function under the chosen NULL intervention; they do not establish biological validity. Clinical evidence relevance achieves AUROC 0.665 against GPT-4 annotations, while expert validation covers only eight query-target pairs per task with one annotator. Broader expert evaluation and attribution stability checks would strengthen the high-stakes usefulness claim.

Clinical outcomes are imperfect proxies for target efficacy: discontinued Phase II/III development is treated as failure despite possible commercial, safety, or molecule-specific causes, as Appendix P acknowledges. Furthermore, no pre-2005 restriction is reported for the genetics associations or GPT-4 knowledge. The temporal interpretation therefore needs to distinguish the literature-only results from augmented and audited variants.

The comparisons do not fully isolate the sources of improvement. Tables 1 and 5 omit a frequency-corrected MLM baseline even though Appendix G provides the corresponding correction. For genetics, a simple semantic-matching baseline would help determine how much improvement comes from replacing ontology similarity, independently of the learned evidence combiner.

Exact experimental reproduction remains constrained by proprietary entity linking, licensed training texts, and the explicit withholding of code and weights. The detailed description supports reimplementation of the core method, but a public-corpus reference configuration and exact GPT-4 versions and generation settings would substantially improve independent verification.

Appendix F contains a substantive derivational mismatch. Section 3.4 excludes the positive entity when sampling negatives, whereas Eq. 9 assumes independent uniform sampling over all entities. With p = P(a|q,L=1) and N entities, the stated sampler gives optimal logit log((N−1)p/(1−p)), rather than log p + log N. Consequently, the exact PMI interpretation in Appendix G needs correction. This does not by itself invalidate the empirical ranking results.
